clue.text: Shame, if many are distressed

indicators.note: distressed letters are knocked about, so the words if many are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone laments the disgrace of many people being upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are distressed' rearranges IFMANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamy is public disgrace or notoriety, the state of being held in shame.

clue.text: Fail to observe fashionable hair-style

parts.note: in means fashionable
a fringe is hair cut across the forehead (US bangs)

explanation.surface: Not noticing a trendy haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: To infringe a rule is to break it rather than comply.

clue.text: As anticipated, the alarm of course was raised

parts.note: fore is the warning shout on a golf course

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word was is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: As expected, the alarm on the course was sounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses WAS to SAW in this down clue. 'of course' suggests 'naturally'; it means on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Foresaw means predicted or expected beforehand.

clue.text: Seam of coal the warship needed?

indicators.note: of ties the seam to the coal, so the layer comes after the mine

parts.note: a coal mine, so coal stands for mine
a seam is a layer of rock or mineral

explanation.surface: A coal seam is just what the navy needed.
explanation.walkthrough: A seam of coal is a layer in a mine. The question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A minelayer is a naval vessel that lays explosive mines at sea.

clue.text: A pleasingly odd-sounding way to give information

indicators.note: the hyphenated odd-sounding tells us the phrase before it is to be heard, not read

parts.note: A, plus pleasingly odd meaning quaint, old-fashioned in a charming way

explanation.surface: A charmingly peculiar way of passing on news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding' says A QUAINT is heard: said aloud it matches the answer. 'way to' just links the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquaint someone with a fact is to inform them of it.

clue.text: Fired revolver

parts.note: not a gun but something set alight that spins round: a firework

explanation.definitionFit: This firework is a spinning wheel that rotates when lit.

clue.text: Extremist takes part in unlawful trade

indicators.note: takes part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A radical is involved in illegal dealing.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is a person with extreme views.

clue.text: Imbecile! I had one of the ears!

parts.note: I'd is short for I had
one is I as a Roman numeral
otic means relating to the ear

explanation.surface: Someone shouts insults and boasts of owning an ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Imbecile' looks like a noun; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Imbecile used as an adjective means stupid, foolish.

clue.text: Ditch where there's fish about, right?

indicators.note: about says the fish goes round the letter for right

parts.note: a tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A ditch where fish swim, is that right?
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TENCH round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow ditch.

clue.text: Great man deigns to accept translation and elevation

indicators.note: translation here means turning words into a new form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A great figure condescends to accept being translated and promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' rearranges GREATMANDEIGNS; 'to accept' and 'and' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggrandisement is the raising of someone in rank, power or importance.

clue.text: Keep nearly half of it, some days

parts.note: a keep is the strongest tower of a castle, here a fort
nigh means nearly

indicators.note: half of a two-letter word is one letter, here the second of it

explanation.surface: An instruction to hold back about half of something for a few days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb; it is the castle stronghold. 'half of' takes T, the second half of IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortnight is a period of two weeks, a set number of days.

clue.text: But wreathe hasn't a double E

parts.note: a double is a twin, one person exactly like another
the letter as printed

explanation.surface: A remark on spelling: the verb wreathe does not contain two Es side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'a double E' as EE; split it instead into 'double' (TWIN) and E. 'But' and 'hasn't' only dress up the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To twine something is to twist or wind it round, as one wreathes flowers.

clue.text: Writer from Napoleonic War is narrow-minded

indicators.note: from here means taken away from the word that follows it

parts.note: the Peninsular War, fought in Spain and Portugal against Napoleon
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A historian of the Napoleonic era turns out to be blinkered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' removes PEN from the start of PENINSULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Insular describes a closed, parochial outlook, like an island cut off from the world.

clue.text: Wild cat lies here, prepared to spring

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the words cat lies are shuffled

explanation.surface: A feral feline crouches here, ready to pounce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges CATLIES. 'here' links fodder and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elastic is springy, ready to bounce back when stretched.

clue.text: Maxim might almost be said to be so awkward

indicators.note: said points to a sound-alike; almost admits the match is close but not exact

parts.note: Maxim Gorky was the Russian writer, so Maxim calls up his surname

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a famous saying could be called clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maxim' looks like a saying; it is Maxim Gorky. In a non-rhotic British accent GORKY sounds close to the answer, hence 'almost'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gawky means ungainly and clumsy, especially of a lanky young person.

clue.text: Annoyance is being put in the shade

indicators.note: being put in says the word before is placed inside the word after

parts.note: a nuance is a shade of meaning or colour

explanation.surface: Irritation at being overshadowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shade' reads as darkness in the surface, but here it is a fine shade of meaning; 'being put in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuisance is something that causes irritation or bother.

clue.text: Snake, one with 100 eyes, swallows a delicacy

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

indicators.note: swallows means the giant takes in the next piece

parts.note: Argus, the hundred-eyed giant of Greek myth

explanation.surface: A many-eyed snake gulps down a choice morsel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallows' puts A inside ARGUS, making ARAGUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus, the vegetable, is a prized and pricey seasonal treat.

clue.text: Deuced is deduce with an amended number

parts.note: to infer is to deduce

indicators.note: amended means changed, so the word an is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A wordplay note: deuced is deduce with letters swapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amended' turns AN into NA. Deuced is an old-fashioned British intensifier, like 'devilish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deuced and the answer are both old intensifiers meaning devilish or damnable.

clue.text: A twopenny increase in value

parts.note: two pennies, p being the abbreviation for a penny
to raise is to increase

explanation.surface: A tiny rise of two pence in the worth of something.
explanation.walkthrough: PP is two pence, p standing for penny.
explanation.definitionFit: To appraise is to assess the worth of something.

clue.text: Father has no use regularly for armour

parts.note: pa is a father
taken as written
to ply a tool is to use it steadily

explanation.surface: Dad has no need of his suit of armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' suggests taking alternate letters; 'use regularly' together means ply.
explanation.definitionFit: A panoply is a complete suit of armour.

clue.text: Type of education required to preserve fruit

parts.note: PE is physical education, a school subject
to can food is to preserve it in tins

explanation.surface: A kind of schooling needed to keep fruit fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required to' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A pecan is a nut, botanically classed as a fruit of the hickory tree.

clue.text: Fancy cooking ham with rice!

indicators.note: cooking means the ingredients ham and rice are mixed up

explanation.surface: A suggestion to cook ham with rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges HAMRICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a fanciful illusion or wild dream.

clue.text: Wet weather clothing on board fishing boats

indicators.note: on board means inside a ship, so the clothing goes inside the letters for ship

parts.note: to be on board is to be on a ship, SS for steamship
a mack, or mac, is a raincoat

explanation.surface: Rainwear on board fishing boats.
explanation.walkthrough: MACK is placed between S and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack is a small sailing boat used for fishing.

clue.text: Creature of the deep, a goddess covered in hair

indicators.note: covered in means the goddess is wrapped by the hair

parts.note: a mane is a long head of hair
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A sea creature, a goddess with flowing locks, like a mermaid.
explanation.walkthrough: Ate is a less familiar Greek goddess; 'covered in' signals the container, and the 'a' before 'goddess' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A manatee is a large aquatic mammal, the sea cow, once taken for a mermaid.

clue.text: Approximately beneath end of elephant's trunk

indicators.note: beneath puts this piece below the other in a down clue
end of picks the final letter of elephant

parts.note: or so means approximately

explanation.surface: Roughly under the end of an elephant's trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' looks like the elephant's; it is the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body.

clue.text: The lady's one to accept a single leading role

parts.note: her is the possessive for a lady

indicators.note: to accept means one takes in the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
a single is one, written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An actress taking a solo starring part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' puts I inside ONE, after its O.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine is the principal female character in a play or story.

clue.text: About a frolic

parts.note: ca is short for circa, meaning about
per means a or each, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: A short phrase about some playful fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' gives PER, as in 'ten pounds a head' = ten pounds per head.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a playful skip or prank.

clue.text: Terrible revenge Queen Bess joined in is not forgotten

indicators.note: joined in says the queen enters the scrambled word
terrible here means mangled, so the word revenge is scrambled

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Elizabeth I's dreadful vengeance remains remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' scrambles revenge into EVGREEN; 'joined in' lets the queen's ER sit after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evergreen stays fresh and popular, never fading from memory.

clue.text: Drunken tinker kicks fox

parts.note: Christopher Sly, the drunken tinker in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew
boots means kicks

explanation.surface: An intoxicated mender of pots lashes out at a fox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fox' looks like an animal; it means a cunning person.
explanation.definitionFit: A slyboots is a crafty, cunning person, as a fox is figuratively.

clue.text: Fall upon a ship feel indisposed afterwards

indicators.note: afterwards puts this piece after the others

parts.note: SS is steamship
to ail is to feel unwell

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a vessel and then feels sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afterwards' places AIL at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack violently.
